raw_general_wording: Incomplete: differentiability, nonnegative decrease and t*f(t)->0 do not imply finite I_f. It is not admitted without the explicit finiteness qualification.
counterexample: f(t)=1/(t logt) on t>=2 satisfies t*f(t)->0 but has divergent integral. The raw real-valued displayed difference is therefore not established.
proof_checks: For continuous monotone f, positive Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure d(-f) gives exact prime-tail Abel summation at inclusive theta(y); differentiability does not silently become absolute continuity.
theta(t)<=constant*t and t*f(t)->0 remove the upper boundary. Integration by parts gives integral t d(-f)=y f(y)+I_f(y), finite after qualification.
Subtracting the same identity with theta(t)=t leaves boundary error bounded by d(y)y f(y), plus integral error bounded by d(y)(y f(y)+I_f(y)), hence exact d(y)(2yf+I_f).

All actual displayed k=2,3 instances use f=t^-k or f=1/(k t^k logt), with root y=x^(1/k) or y=x>1. These are smooth nonnegative decreasing kernels; their finite integrals are bounded exactly as written.

The inverse-log kernel substitution w=(k-1)logt gives I_f(y)=E1((k-1)logy)/k; at root y=x^(1/k) this is E1((1-1/k)L)/k. At y=x, the lower limit is (k-1)L. No unrooted source onset is transferred to a root.
For those smooth kernels d(-f)=-fprime dt, so every actual old formula/consumer retains its original execution and numerical output; no new analytic-source premise is introduced.
